official.title: PhD Positions on Silicon-Carbide Quantum Networks
official.description_text:
Job description
We are recruiting several PhD candidates to join the Taminiau lab in research on quantum networks based on spin defects in silicon carbide (SiC). As a part of the team, you will work alongside scientists to investigate and develop SiC devices that enable fast optical entanglement links and high-fidelity spin-qubit control. The research combines the design and fabrication of nano-photonic SiC devices, with quantum optics experiments to demonstrate small, but scalable, quantum networks for distributed quantum computation, simulations, and communication.
The Taminiau Lab is an international and collaborative group where people from different backgrounds work closely together, share ideas openly, and support each other's development. We value diversity, teamwork, and creating an environment where everyone can contribute and grow.
Requirements
You have a MSc in science in (applied) physics, quantum technologies, material science, or a related field.
You are highly motivated to work on the nano fabrication and characterization of quantum devices for quantum networks.
Relevant experience in device fabrication, nanophotonics and/or experimental quantum physics (e.g. with spins or superconducting systems) are appreciated but not essential.
TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.
For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.
At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.
QuTech
At QuTech, we work on radically new technologies with world-changing potential. Our mission: to develop scalable prototypes of a quantum computer and a quantum internet by integrating world-class research and groundbreaking innovation. Through excellence, relevance, and leadership, we cultivate a vibrant quantum technology ecosystem. Together, we are creating the quantum future, because we believe that quantum technologies can be a game changer in many societal and economic sectors, including health, agriculture and safety.
Have a look at our
video
and get a glimpse of QuTech.
Conditions of employment
Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met.
Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%.
As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills.
The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged.
Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit,
Coming to Delft Service
, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A
Dual Career Programme
is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands.
Additional information
For more information about this vacancy, please contact Dr, Tim Taminiau at
T.H.Taminiau@TUDelft.nl
. Group website:
https://taminiaulab.qutech.nl
.
Application procedure
Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than
15 December 2026
via the application button and upload the following documents:
CV
Motivational letter
You can address your application to Dr. Tim Taminiau.
Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the
Graduate Schools Admission Requirements.
Please note:
You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post.
As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about
knowledge security.
Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

ai.summary: PhD positions in quantum networks based on spin defects in silicon carbide (SiC). Research focuses on nano-photonic device design and fabrication, quantum optics experiments, and demonstration of scalable quantum networks for distributed quantum computation, simulation, and communication.

thematic_fit.rationale: Research is quantum technology (device fabrication, nanophotonics, quantum optics) for quantum computing and communication networks. 'Networks' refers to quantum entanglement distribution, not social or collaborative human systems. No connection to human-centred immersive systems, spatial learning, collaborative interaction, or HCI. Fundamentally a quantum device/materials science position.

methodological_fit.rationale: Position requires nano-fabrication, device characterization, quantum optics measurement, and nanophotonic design. Researcher's methodology (user studies, human-factors experimental design, task evaluation) does not transfer. Quantum device development and nano-fabrication are entirely distinct research practices from HCI experimental methodology.

growth_value.rationale: This would develop expertise in quantum device fabrication, nanophotonics, and quantum optics. Researcher's identified capability gaps (statistics for human-centred analysis, physiological sensing, eye-tracking, mixed-effects modelling) are orthogonal. Growth trajectory is away from human-centred research priorities and stated target identity.

strategic_value.rationale: TU Delft is priority-2 (Netherlands, strong institution). QuTech is well-funded and internationally visible. However, the group's mission is quantum technology development, not human-centred research. Supervision would be in nanophotonics and quantum optics. Peer network would be quantum engineers and device physicists. Limited strategic value for transitioning to human-centred XR research ecosystems.

eligibility_flags: Position requires MSc in (applied) physics, quantum technologies, material science, or related field. Researcher holds MSc by Research in Creative Multimedia. Field not listed as qualifying; eligibility contingent on demonstrating equivalent physics/materials science foundation.

Posting notes 'relevant experience in device fabrication, nanophotonics and/or experimental quantum physics are appreciated but not essential.' While not strictly required, absence of nano-fabrication or nanophotonics background is a disadvantage relative to typical applicant pool.

Position targets candidates with motivation for 'nano fabrication and characterization of quantum devices.' Researcher shows no documented interest in nano-fabrication, device characterization, or quantum systems work.
risks: Research domain (quantum networks, nanophotonics, SiC devices) is entirely separate from human-centred XR. This is a pure quantum technology position masquerading as slightly less esoteric because it mentions 'networks'—but quantum networks are not collaborative human systems.

Position exemplifies excluded research directions: pure technical device engineering and physics, no human-centred evaluation, no learning outcomes, no human factors. Accepting contradicts stated excluded directions.

Nano-fabrication and quantum-device work requires sustained technical specialization. A PhD in this area (4 years typical) would deeply embed researcher in quantum technology rather than human-centred XR.
Supervision and peer network would be quantum physicists, device engineers, and nanophotonics specialists. Limited cross-disciplinary exposure to HCI, design science, or human-factors research.

Future transition back to human-centred XR research would require re-establishing HCI credibility. Career trajectory would appear unfocused or redirected rather than coherent progression toward stated target identity.

This position offers no pathway to human-centred XR communities or supervision networks, despite being at a target institution (Delft). Institutional location is misleading; research direction is fundamentally misaligned.
